core_obligations: Part (1) (proof lines 4415-4418): the value of the direct image of a representable presheaf at an object is computed by the adjunction.

Parts (2) and (3) (proof lines 4421-4436): the unit and the counit of the adjunction provide initial and final objects of the auxiliary categories, and the author verifies the universal properties explicitly.

Parts (4) and (5) (proof lines 4438-4453): the identification of the functors is obtained by another computation with representables and adjunctions, and the last assertion follows from the uniqueness of adjoint functors.
proof_roadmap: Compute the direct image of a representable presheaf using the adjunction.
Produce and verify initial and final objects of the auxiliary categories using the unit and the counit.
Identify the functors on presheaves and invoke uniqueness of adjoints.
difficulty_reason: The lemma collects five consequences of a functor being right adjoint to another: the direct image of a representable presheaf is representable, two auxiliary categories of morphisms have initial respectively final objects, and the functors on presheaves are identified with the corresponding functors attached to the adjoint (statement lines 4400-4412). The proof treats the parts in turn: part (1) is an adjunction computation (proof lines 4415-4418); parts (2) and (3) exhibit the initial and final objects through the unit and counit and verify their universal properties (proof lines 4421-4436); parts (4) and (5) are further adjunction computations and a uniqueness argument (proof lines 4438-4453). The non-formal content is the two explicit computations. The claim is H1/H2: five short verifications, each written out.
